rules.title: Low reading level or limited literacy
guidance: Do not include written labels, captions, letters, numbers, or speech bubbles.
Use concrete objects and visible actions instead of symbolic text.
sourceBasis: ASHA AAC: symbol type, display features, language/literacy level should be individualized.
cardPlanningActions: Prefer picture/object symbols over printed labels.
Keep Korean sentence editable for teacher but out of generated image.

rules.title: Short attention span
guidance: Show one concept and one main object per card.
Remove decorative background details and competing secondary actions.
sourceBasis: CAST UDL: representation and engagement should reduce barriers for learner variability.
cardPlanningActions: Remove secondary actions.
Use one focal noun and one focal verb per card.

rules.title: Cause-effect support
guidance: Represent cause and effect with a single thick arrow from cause to result.
Use before-after or input-output structure when the science concept changes state.
sourceBasis: WWC learning guide: connect abstract and concrete representations and combine graphics with verbal descriptions.
cardPlanningActions: Split cause and result into neighboring cards.
Use one arrow from cause to effect.

rules.title: Abstract concept support
guidance: Anchor invisible science ideas in familiar visible examples, such as leaves, water drops, sun, magnets, arrows, or simple particles.
Avoid metaphors that require extra background knowledge.
sourceBasis: WWC learning guide: connect abstract representations with concrete representations.
cardPlanningActions: Map invisible science terms to visible anchors.
Prefer familiar classroom objects.

rules.title: Emotional and behavioral support
guidance: Use calm, predictable layouts with friendly neutral facial expressions only when a face is necessary.
Avoid danger, clutter, exaggerated emotion, punishment imagery, or startling motion cues.
sourceBasis: Visual supports evidence: visual supports clarify routines, transitions, academics, and behavior expectations.
cardPlanningActions: Use predictable sequence order.
Avoid startling emotion or threat imagery.

rules.title: Receptive language support with one-clause Korean sentences
guidance: Use one independent clause per card and avoid embedded clauses or conditional clauses.
Prefer Korean subject-object-verb card text such as “잎이 햇빛을 받는다.” and avoid two verbs in one sentence.
cardPlanningActions: Choose one subject, one object, and one predicate from curriculum decomposition hints.
If the source has two verbs, split it into two cards.
sourceBasis: CAST UDL: language/symbol representation and comprehension supports.
ASHA AAC: receptive language and command-following are part of AAC assessment.

rules.title: Working-memory load limit
guidance: Keep the storyboard to three or four cards and make each card independently understandable.
Do not require the student to remember hidden information from a previous card to understand the next card.
cardPlanningActions: Repeat the science subject across adjacent cards when the object changes.
Avoid pronouns like 이것/그것 if the referent may be unclear.
sourceBasis: ASHA AAC: cognitive communication assessment includes memory, attention, problem-solving, and executive skills.
WWC: combine graphics with verbal descriptions for key processes.

rules.title: Visual discrimination and figure-ground support
guidance: Use a clean white field, a single focal object, high contrast, and generous spacing.
Avoid grids, multiple competing symbols, decorative backgrounds, and tiny details.
cardPlanningActions: Use one object/action per image prompt.
Prefer large centered symbols and thick outlines.
sourceBasis: ASHA AAC: symbol size, field size, visual acuity, and sensory status should guide display design.
Visual supports evidence: visuals clarify environments, instructions, academics, and behavior.

rules.title: Predictable sequence for transition or emotional regulation needs
guidance: Use a stable first-next-then sequence and keep card layout consistent.
Avoid surprise outcomes; show what changes before showing the result.
cardPlanningActions: Order cards as input, action/change, result.
Keep border and visual style consistent across all cards.
sourceBasis: ASHA ID: activity schedules and visual supports can help individuals complete sequences, attend to tasks, and transition between activities.
CAST UDL: engagement includes sustaining effort and self-regulation.

rules.title: Core vocabulary reuse for AAC consistency
guidance: Reuse stable high-frequency Korean predicates such as 받는다, 간다, 만든다, 바뀐다, 먹는다, 돈다.
Keep the same concept visually similar across regenerated cards.
cardPlanningActions: Prefer curriculum cardSentenceFrames over novel paraphrases.
Use the same noun for the same science object across cards.
sourceBasis: ASHA AAC: core vocabulary supports multiple communicative functions and symbol organization may minimize memory and motor-planning demands.
